notes: Behaviour is correct, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, and its tests are unit-level only with no retry-path integration test.

Behaves correctly, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy placeholder names and an IsResponseCondition concept into the generic CEL matcher, and only unit-tests the predicate with no proxy-level regression test.

Correct AST-based approach with a predicate API and good unit and integration tests, including a ph() response retry; the provisioning helper appends to receiver fields, and the RetryMatch doc rewrite is extra but justified.

Nice predicate-based ReferencesPlaceholders API with correct handling of dynamic names; the tests are good, but one test comment wrongly says latency isn't response data, and the provision step appends rather than resets.

Generic ReferencedPlaceholders API in the CEL matcher with the response-placeholder policy kept in reverseproxy; it has a helpful doc update and strong integration tests covering request-only forms, shorthand vs direct ph(), and dynamic names.

Clean generic ReferencedPlaceholders API with response placeholder constants in reverseproxy and an accurate RetryMatch doc update; integration tables cover every case the spec calls out, though comments are somewhat verbose.

The AST check works, but it is OR-ed with a ~250-line hand-written text scanner of the raw expression that duplicates logic and can produce false positives, adds several dead alias functions apparently written to guess hidden test names, and duplicates isResponsePlaceholder across packages.

Adds a redundant ~250-line hand-written text parser ORed with the AST check (causing false positives, e.g. 'ph(req, x)' inside a string literal), unused alias functions apparently meant to guess test names, needless rp.* names and a duplicated helper.

Correct, with sensible constant-folding of literal concatenations, but it also places reverse_proxy policy inside the generic CEL matcher and includes an odd 'appeasing the linter' switch arm; it adds a good unit table and one integration test.

Correct AST-based detection that also folds constant string concatenation, but it puts reverse-proxy placeholder knowledge and a response-specific method into the generic caddyhttp matcher; it has a good unit table and an integration test.

Collects literal ph() names and a dynamic flag from the checked AST, then checks them against the exact response placeholders and the header prefix in reverseproxy; it closely matches the reference, has thorough unit and integration tests, and its only nit is that Placeholders() returns the internal slice uncloned.

Closely mirrors the reference: a generic Placeholders() accessor (built with MatchDescendants) feeds a reverse-proxy-local response list, backed by thorough unit tables and an integration test that also verifies the request body.

Clean AST-based extraction with a predicate API (ReferencesPlaceholder) that keeps reverse-proxy knowledge in reverseproxy, plus a broad table test that covers comprehensions and lookalikes and an end-to-end test that echoes the body.
Concise and idiomatic (ReferencesPlaceholder with slices.ContainsFunc), with a comprehensive matcherSet table covering the spec cases plus macros and lookalikes, and an end-to-end body-echo test.

Keeps the caller cancelling while a child is unfinished, but shares C2's same-value rewrite / 0-rows issue and the set-then-override status logic is clumsy; it returns an error from cancelRun after the transaction has committed if the emit fails, though its end-to-end service test is strong.

Hard-codes Cancelling for a caller with unfinished children rather than aggregating, and makes cancelRun return an error when the emit fails after the transaction has already committed; the integration test does show the waiter starting.

Re-aggregates a caller from its children in cancelOneJob, so callers stay cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and emits after settling; it also extends force-cancel to settle a run whose cascade stops at an already-final caller, which is useful but goes slightly past the issue, and the caller is returned even when unchanged.

Aggregates callers from their children (with a small justified refactor to avoid refetching them), also settles force-cancelled runs whose cascade stops at an already-final caller, and covers both stuck variants with thorough tests.

Correctly keeps a caller cancelling while any child is unfinished and emits after a no-job settle; but it rewrites a status the child cascade already set, which on MySQL/MariaDB can report 0 affected rows, log a spurious error and drop the caller from updatedJobs, and it still forces Cancelled rather than aggregating once all children are done.

Hard-codes Cancelling with a separate guarded update that can hit the 'changed' error path when the cascade already wrote the same value; it works, but is less robust than aggregating, and the test sets up data with raw SQL.

Correct caller re-aggregation and an extra force-settle path for stuck runs, with excellent end-to-end tests; however it emits EmitJobsIfReadyByRun after every cancel unconditionally (redundant queue work) and the force-settle change widens scope.

The caller re-aggregation in cancelReusableCaller and the force settle are sound, but it emits the run unconditionally on every cancel, which is redundant and contradicts its own comment; tests are good.

Sound fix that aggregates the caller from its children and emits only when a previously unfinished run was settled; the model test is thorough (including attempt status), but there is no test for the service-side concurrency emit and the reloaded caller is returned even when unchanged.

Always aggregates an expanded caller from its children, which is a principled fix, and triggers the emitter only when the run was actually settled; its nested test is solid, but there is no test for releasing the concurrency group.

Re-aggregates a caller only when a direct child is Cancelling, which covers the reported nested case but is a narrower trigger than full aggregation; the emit-after-settle mirrors the reference and the tests are solid.

Keeps a caller cancelling by re-aggregating it in cancelOneJob when any direct child is still cancelling, and emits on a settled run when no job was updated; minimal and correct, though it always returns the reloaded caller even when its status did not change.

Closest to the reference: it routes expanded callers through a reload-and-reaggregate helper and returns them only when their status changed, and emits after a settle that leaves the run done; the service test only checks the mocked emit, not that the waiting run is released.

Closely mirrors the reference: it reloads each expanded caller, re-aggregates it and compares against the stale row, plus a well-targeted emit after settling; the service test only checks that the emit was called.
